basis: Congenital structural abnormalities of the kidneys and urinary tract define this disease.
Inherited hypercatabolism of albumin and IgG with immunodeficiency; bronchiectasis in 2/2 supports pulmonary damage.
Mature T-cell lymphoma; extranodal sites vary across subtypes, with no additional organ consistently affected across the umbrella.
Ulceration confined to the vulva, a reproductive organ outside the axes; no specific infectious or immune mechanism established.
Malignant lymphoid-cell neoplasm; no particular extranodal organ is established as commonly damaged.
Brain and urinary tract malformations define the syndrome; reflux 30-79%. Metopic craniosynostosis in 1/1 supports skeletal involvement, with limited sampling.
Inherited cone and rod photoreceptor degeneration confined to the retina.
Hyperlipoproteinemia and hearing loss define the syndrome; atherosclerosis is a separate disease, and corneal arcus does not impair vision.
Benign smooth-muscle tumour arising in the uterine wall; reproductive organs have no axis.
Skeletal malformations and intellectual/developmental disability define it; ptosis 80-99% supports eyelid dysfunction. Dental crowding alone does not establish oral damage.
Congenital fistula directly connects the malformed rectum with the prostatic urethra; both structures define the disease.
Bile-duct-derived liver cysts define it. Renal cysts occur in 14/25, but the definition describes them as incidental without functional renal damage.
MSRB3-related nonsyndromic hearing loss; no extra-auditory disease is established.
Limb reduction defects, ear malformations with conductive deafness, and sinus arrhythmia are defining components.
Developmental speech-fluency disorder; communication and neurodevelopmental dysfunction fall within the neurologic axis.
Fungal infection directly inflames and damages an intervertebral disc.
Deficiency-related anemia is defined by impaired red-cell production or hemoglobin; no additional organ damage applies across the umbrella.
Intellectual disability and epilepsy define it; strabismus and congenital muscular torticollis each occur in 1/3, supporting eye and muscle involvement with limited sampling.
Inherited platelet dysfunction and early gastrointestinal mucosal ulceration are defining features; altered eicosanoids do not independently establish endocrine disease.
Neurodevelopmental dysfunction and cortical dysplasia define the main phenotype; listed ocular, cardiac and other structural defects are individually below 30%.
Patellar aplasia and microtia define it; speech/motor delay 2/3; emphysema and airway malacia 1/3 support pulmonary damage. Reflux is separately diagnosed.
Congenital digit shortening, fusion and absence are skeletal malformations; no extra-skeletal involvement is supplied.
Postsynaptic neuromuscular-junction dysfunction; weakness and ptosis reflect transmission failure, not independent muscle or eye damage. Respiratory distress is 1/4.
Hepatitis E virus directly causes liver inflammation; extrahepatic injury is not common enough to qualify.
Lower motor-neuron disease with characteristic proximal lower-limb denervation and muscle atrophy in most affected patients.
